blocks.text: In October 1975, staff at the DSIR Physics and Engineering Laboratory processed Landsat II imagery using computer-compatible tapes, IBM mainframe processing, minicomputers and programs written in PL/I. Specialists rectified, classified and interpreted the imagery, working within the limitations of the available computers and image-processing software. Each scene required considerable technical work before it could contribute to mapping or environmental analysis.

blocks.text: By the 2020s, New Zealand analysts could obtain repeated satellite observations, national mosaics and land-cover datasets through established data services. Online archives and processing software allowed them to examine imagery from many dates and use it alongside other spatial information. Repeated acquisitions and sustained data maintenance supported routine environmental monitoring, while aerial photography continued to serve applications requiring different detail and timing.
